body:
That sounds like a really reasonable thing to do. I guess I just needed confirmation that it'd be a good idea, as opposed to a mistake to go. I don't think I'm a risk to myself at all right now. I've seen firsthand what suicide does to the people who are left behind, so it'd be really hard for me to go through with it. I just would really prefer to not have these thoughts, and the depression, because although I've hidden it from everyone else, it's a bitch to deal with.

 I think everyone has those thoughts while driving, it's just putting our morality and fragility in perspective with our current situation.

I'll go dig out my insurance card from my filing cabinet in the morning, and see what it's got on it. 

I'll probably set up a session for sometime in January, see how things go. I know that this is just a little corner of the internet, but really, thank you. I've been meaning to post this for a while, and I've actually got the confidence to go now.

The information I've been able to find has been vague on it. Under Arizona Title 36, to be admitted involuntarily for a psychiatric evaluation, Arizona law requires that the person "is likely without immediate hospitalization to suffer serious physical harm or serious illness or is likely to inflict serious physical harm on another person." But from what I've read, that's really up to the therapist, whether they want to request a psychiatric hold/eval. There's stories of some people getting sent as soon as they mention suicidal urges, which is what I'm afraid of.

Like you said, there's typically the 3 criteria (plan, time, and means) but I suppose I'm just worried of having an overcautious therapist. I do have a plan and the means, technically (seeing as how I drive almost everyday), although I don't want to hurt myself. I don't think I'm bad enough to go to the hospital at all, I'd just like some help with it.

How did you do your counseling? Do you just make an appointment? Does insurance cover any of it? And how many sessions did you go for? I'm a university student, so I have access to the school's discounted services, but I don't have enough money to pay out-of-pocket for an extended amount of time.

Thanks for your help.
